chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), regarding
an insane woman who committed adultery. He said: 'She has no control over her affair, and there is nothing upon her.'

key_terms.لَا تَمْلِكُ أَمْرَهَا: she has no control over her affair/matter
key_terms.مَجْنُونَةٍ: insane woman (one lacking full mental capacity)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling for an insane person who commits adultery in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that an insane woman is exempt from hadd penalties for adultery because she lacks full legal capacity (ahliyyah), as she 'has no control over her affair.' This ruling aligns with the broader Shia jurisprudential principle that the 'pen of lifting' applies to the insane, distinguishing their civil liability from that of the sane. It underscores the mercy in Islamic law by removing punitive burden where cognitive control is absent.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated either) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) regarding
an insane woman who committed adultery. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘She had no control over her affair, and there is nothing upon her’.
